audit_scope.mathematical: Complete three-unit actual-file proof read. One geometric generic hyperplane detects every original cover without a simultaneous closed-point choice. Formal branches over exceptional fibres factor through the fixed original complete local puncture or divisor pair, while strict-transform branches lie over the generic original boundary point and are tame cyclic. Surjective precomposition preserves projective conjugacy injection. The fixed-source local counts and fixed-full-local-type affine curve theorem give the claimed unrestricted global PGL count, with controlled-boundary and simple-product consequences in their stated scopes.
checks: A height-one completed branch containing the original divisor ideal has nonzero contraction. That contraction cannot be the maximal ideal because its extension is the completed maximal ideal of height two. Thus the contraction is height one and the two localizations are DVRs.
Faithful flatness of completion supplies the DVR inclusion. Tameness is preserved for an arbitrary extension of DVRs; no finite residue-extension or perfect-residue hypothesis is imposed.

At a generic strict-transform intersection, algebraic independence of the hyperplane coefficients excludes every original closed k-point. The formal branch therefore lies over the original boundary generic point; transversality gives the uniformizer order one.
Rank-independent highest-break bounds use the original pair conductor theorem and a faithful regular representation of each finite quotient. No conductor estimate is inferred merely from rank.
Only the affine detecting-curve theorem uses a same-field GL lift. No global H2 inflation or Brauer vanishing is asserted.
The defining-characteristic simple-product argument uses the already audited faithful projective embeddings and order bounds; it does not extend a nonabelian crown theorem.
